newsitem.title: FRANCE: French opposition parties hail Thomson reversal.
newsitem.headline: French opposition parties hail Thomson reversal.

text.p: French opposition parties on Wednesday revelled in the government's decision to suspend the controversial privatisation of electronics group Thomson SA and said they hoped the entire plan would now be scrapped.
"Today, it is a first success ... but we should not stop there," Socialist Party spokesman Francois Hollande said after the weekly meeting of the party's national leadership.
"We have to make sure that after this first victory.. the government continue this bad job after December 31," he said.
"We are now calling for the privatisation to be abandoned totally," Hollande said.

He said the privatisation's suspension was the result of strong opposition by the staff of Thomson and left-wing political parties and called it a "serious disaster" for the government of conservative Prime Minister Alain Juppe.
Juppe's government on Wednesday froze the sale of Thomson after an independent privatisation commission objected to plans to sell part of the company to South Korean Daewoo.

It was the second sell-off to be halted in less than a month and came at a time when Prime Minister Alain Juppe, at a record low in opinion polls, is anxious to avoid another labour revolt following last month's truckers stoppage.
Hollande accused the centre-right government of bungling the sale politically as well as technically.
But Juppe's RPR Gaullist party hit back, saying Thomson's problems resulted mainly from 28 billion francs ($5.3 billion) of debts piled up after nationalisation by the Socialists in the early 1980s.
Hollande was behaving like a "shipwrecked man who blames his rescuers for his problems in getting afloat," the RPR said.
Parliamentarians of the Communist Party said they now wanted a national debate on the future of Thomson.

"The privatisation commission, by giving a negative opinion on the acquisition of Thomson Multimedia by the South Korean company Daewoo (Electronics ), is contradicting the choice of the government," the parliamentary group said.
It said the suspension was "a great encouragement for all the staff of the company to continue the struggle they have been leading for many months to safeguard the integrity of the state company".
The leftist Force Ouvriere union said the privatisation had been doomed to fail by the way it had been set up.
It said it was strongly opposed to a sale of Thomson Multimedia to Korea's Daewoo and called on the government to study the project again on a "more serious basis".
As long as uncertainty remained over what would happen, Thomson jobs were being put at risk, it said.
France's largest trade union, the Socialist-backed CFDT, said it would continue to campaign for the preservation of jobs at Thomson. ($ = 5.270 French Francs)
